36 	
37 	</details>

19 	
20 	Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
21 	
22 	With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), a [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) prefetches one reusable [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route by default. The App Shell includes the route's static output. For routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), it also includes session-specific UI. Links to the same route reuse that App Shell.
23 	
24 	The shared App Shell does not include URL data that varies by destination, such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional). Set `prefetch={true}` on a link to resolve cached content that depends on its [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) before navigation instead of streaming that content after navigation.
25 	
26 	This guide assumes [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled:
27 	
28 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5}
29 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
30 	
31 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
32 	  cacheComponents: true,
33 	  partialPrefetching: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	export default nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	It also assumes your route is already structured for instant navigation. If it isn't, start with the [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) to validate its caching structure first.
40 	
41 	## Resolve URL data at prefetch time
42 	
43 	Set `<Link prefetch={true}>` to resolve URL data for that link before navigation. The destination must use [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), enabled globally with `partialPrefetching` or per segment with [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch#partial).
44 	
45 	A user on `/` sees links to `/search?q=react` and `/search?q=next`, each opting in with `prefetch={true}`:
46 	
47 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
48 	import Link from 'next/link'
49 	
50 	export default function Home() {
51 	  return (
52 	    <nav>
53 	      <Link href="/search?q=react" prefetch={true}>
54 	        React
55 	      </Link>
56 	      <Link href="/search?q=next" prefetch={true}>
57 	        Next.js
58 	      </Link>
59 	    </nav>
60 	  )
61 	}

Now I have the complete picture and the exact right primitive. Let me design the solution precisely.

**Design decision: `navigation()` is the correct primitive.**

The user wants:
1. Title appears instantly on navigation from the dashboard.
2. The rest of the project page is NOT prefetched.

The `navigation()` function defers content below it so it renders only on the actual navigation, not in any prefetch. The title (above `navigation()`, cached) renders in the prefetch/shell, so it appears instantly. The details (below `navigation()`) render only when the user navigates — not prefetched.

But there's a critical subtlety about the title being "instant." The title depends on `params` (URL data, the slug). Per the docs, content depending on `params`/`searchParams` is "already left out of the shell on its own" (from the `prefetch()` doc: "Uncached reads, values with a short stale time, and anything behind `params` or `searchParams` are already left out of the shell on their own"). So with a default `<Link>` (no `prefetch={true}`), the title — which depends on `params` — would NOT be in the App Shell and would stream in on navigation, not appear "instantly."

Wait — but the user wants the title to appear *instantly*. There are two interpretations:
- **(A)** "Instantly" = on click, with no round-trip wait (i.e., prefetched so it's there the moment you click). This requires the title to be prefetched, which for URL-dependent content needs `<Link prefetch={true}>`. But the user said don't prefetch the *rest* — the title is fine to prefetch.
- **(B)** "Instantly" = the title is the first thing to resolve/stream, ahead of the slow details (800ms). The loading fallback shows the title immediately while details stream.

Given the phrasing "appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page," the most faithful reading is: prefetch the title (so it's instant on click), do NOT prefetch the rest. That maps to: `<Link prefetch={true}>` on the dashboard + `navigation()` on the details so the details are excluded even from the per-link prefetch.

Let me verify this combination works: with `partialPrefetching` enabled, `<Link prefetch={true}>` resolves URL data + cached content. The title (`getProjectTitle`, cached with `'use cache'`) depends on `params` — with `prefetch={true}` it gets resolved in the per-link prefetch and is instant on click. The details component calls `navigation()`, which keeps it out of *both* the App Shell and per-link prefetch, so it renders only on navigation. This satisfies both requirements precisely.

However, there's the question of whether to enable `partialPrefetching` globally. The `navigation()` function "is meant for routes using Partial Prefetching" but also: "Without Partial Prefetching, `navigation()` still defers the content for a default `<Link>`, but `<Link prefetch={true}>` fetches the whole route, deferred content included, the same as a navigation." 

That's the key constraint: **without `partialPrefetching`, a `<Link prefetch={true}>` would fetch the whole route including the deferred details** — defeating "don't prefetch the rest." So to both prefetch the title (via `prefetch={true}`) AND exclude the details from that prefetch, I MUST enable `partialPrefetching`.

So the complete solution:
1. Enable `partialPrefetching: true` in `next.config.ts`.
2. Split the project page: title in one Suspense (cached, in prefetch), details in another Suspense with `navigation()` to keep them out of prefetches.
3. Use `<Link prefetch={true}>` on the dashboard so the title resolves before navigation (instant on click), while `navigation()` keeps the details out of that prefetch.

Let me confirm the title's `getProjectTitle` cache staleness is adequate for the App Shell (the docs mention a 5-minute stale threshold). Let me check the `use cache` default profile and `cacheLife` doc briefly, and the `instant` route segment config.

17 	The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. 24 	
25 	## Usage

27 	`use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file:

34 	}

37 	```

## What changed and why

The goal: the project title appears instantly when navigating from the dashboard, but the rest of the project page is not prefetched. This Next.js 16 canary uses Cache Components, so I followed the dist/docs/ guides (instant-navigation, optimizing-prefetching, and the navigation()/prefetch() API references) rather than legacy patterns.

1. next.config.ts — enabled partialPrefetching: true.
This is required for the combination to work. Without it, a <Link prefetch={true}> fetches the entire route (deferred content included), which would defeat "don't prefetch the rest." With it, prefetching splits into an App Shell + an optional per-link prefetch that resolves URL data, and navigation() can exclude content from both.

2. app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx — split the single <Suspense> into two:
- <ProjectTitle> — cached (getProjectTitle uses 'use cache', default 5-min stale), depends on params. It sits above any deferral, so a per-link prefetch resolves it and it renders instantly on click.
- <ProjectDetails> — calls await navigation() before reading params/fetching. Per the navigation() docs, this keeps everything below it out of the App Shell and out of per-link prefetches, so the description + activity list render only when the user actually navigates, never prefetched.

3. app/page.tsx — added prefetch={true} to the dashboard <Link>s.
The title depends on params (URL data), which is excluded from the shared App Shell by default. prefetch={true} opts into a per-link prefetch that resolves that URL-data-dependent, cached title before navigation — so it's instant on click. The details are still excluded from that prefetch by navigation().

- npx tsc --noEmit → exit 0, no errors (after the build generated .next/types for the PageProps global).

One thing to note: navigation() (and the per-link prefetch) only take effect in production (next start); Next.js does not perform prefetches in next dev, so in dev the details will resolve on navigation rather than being held back by a prefetch. The structure is correct for production.
